name: Sikaflex-116 High Grab
paste:
SIKAFLEX®-116 HIGH GRAB: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikaflex®-116 High Grab, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/v/sikaflex-116-highgrab.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikaflex®-116 High Grab where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sikaflex®-116 High Grab is a construction adhesive with high initial grab which bonds most construction material substrates.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. An adhesive to bond construction components and materials such as:
    - Concrete
    - Masonry
    - Most stones
    - Ceramic
    - Wood
    - Metals
    - Glass
    - Mirrors*
    For interior and exterior use
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.6.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikaflex®-116 High Grab
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: High Grab Construction Adhesive
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - Conformity with LEED v4 EQc 2: Low-Emitting Materials
    - VOC emission classification GEV-Emicode EC1PLUS, license number 11489/20.10.00
    - VOC emission classification of building materials RTS M1
    - Class A+ according to French Regulation on VOC emissions
2.3 Approvals / certificates.
    - CE Marking and Declaration of Performance to EN 15651-1 - Sealants for non-structural use in joints in buildings - Facade elements: Class F EXT-INT CC 20HM
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 15651-1: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - ISO 1183-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.1).
    - ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore A hardness (p.2).
    - ISO 7390: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Sag flow (p.2).
    - CQP 019-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Skinning time (p.2).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - High initial grab
    - Fixing of heavy items without temporary fixation
    - Good workability
    - Very low emissions
    - Adhesive-sealant with CE marking
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Silane terminated polymer
    - Colour: White
    - Density: ~1.40 kg/l (ISO 1183-1)
2.7 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: ~45 (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Tensile strength: ~2.2 N/mm² (ISO 37)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~500 % (ISO 37)
    - Tear propagation resistance: ~7.0 N/mm (ISO 34)
    - Service temperature: −40 °C min. / +80 °C max.
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 290 ml cartridge: 12 cartridges per box
    - Shelf life: 12 months from the date of production
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +25 °C. Always refer to packaging.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be sound, clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, cement laitance, old sealants and poorly bonded paint coatings which could affect adhesion of the adhesive.
    - For optimum adhesion and critical, high performance applications the following priming and/or pre-treatment procedures must be followed:
    - Non-porous substrates
    - Aluminium, anodised aluminium, stainless steel, galvanised steel, powder coated metals or glazed tiles, slightly roughen surface with a fine abrasive pad. Clean and pre-treat using Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth.
    - Before bonding / sealing, allow a waiting time of > 15 minutes (< 6 hours).
    - Other metals, such as copper, brass and titanium-zinc, clean and pre-treat using Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth. After a waiting time of > 15 minutes (< 6 hours). Apply Sika® Primer-3 N applied by brush. Allow a further waiting time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours) before bonding / sealing.
    - PVC has to be cleaned and pre-treated using Sika® Primer-215 applied with a brush. Allow a waiting time of > 15 minutes (< 8 hours) before bonding / sealing. Porous substrates
    - Concrete, aerated concrete and cement based renders, mortars and bricks, prime surface using Sika® Primer-3 N applied by brush.
    - Before bonding / sealing, allow a waiting time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours).
    - For more detailed advice and instructions contact Sika Technical Services.
    - Note: Primers are adhesion promoters and not an alternative to improve poor preparation / cleaning of joint surfaces. Primers also improve the long term adhesion performance of a sealed joint.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Sag flow: 0 mm (20 mm profile, 23 °C) (ISO 7390)
    - Curing rate: ~3 mm/24 hours (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.); *Sika Corporate Quality Procedure (CQP* 049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~20 min (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
4.3 Yield.
    | Yield | Dimension |
    | 1 Cartridge (290 ml) |
    | ~100 spots | Diameter = 30 mm |
    | Thickness = 4 mm |
    | ~5 m bead * | Nozzle diameter = 5 mm |
    | (~60 ml per linear meter) |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    * Note: For heavy items more or thicker beads (up to ~120 ml per linear metre) maybe required.
    These figures are theoretical and do not allow for any additional material due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level or wastage etc.
4.4 Application method / tools - Bonding Procedure.
    - After the necessary substrate preparation, prepare the end of the cartridge before or after inserting into a trade quality sealant gun then fit the nozzle.
    - Apply in beads, strips or spots at intervals of a few centimetres each. Use hand pressure only to fix the components to be bonded into position before skinning of the adhesive occurs. Incorrectly positioned components can easily be unbonded and repositioned during the first few minutes after application. If necessary, use temporary adhesive tapes, wedges, or supports to hold the assembled components together during the initial curing time.
    - Fresh, uncured adhesive remaining on the surface must be removed immediately. Final strength will be reached after complete curing of Sikaflex®-116 High Grab, i.e. after 24 to 48 hours at +23 °C, depending on the environmental conditions and adhesive layer thickness.
4.5 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment immediately after use with Sika® Remover-208. Once cured, hardened material can only be removed mechanically. For cleaning skin use Sika® Cleaning Wipes.
4.6 Limitations and important considerations.
    - *For mirror bonding, do not use over vinyl backing.
    - For optimum workability, the recommended adhesive temperature is +20 °C.
    - Application during high temperature changes is not recommended (movement during the curing).
    - Before bonding, check adhesion and compatibility of paints and coatings by carrying out preliminary trials.
    - Sikaflex®-116 High Grab can be overpainted with most conventional water-based coating and paint systems. However, they must first be tested to ensure compatibility by carrying out preliminary trials. The best over-painting results are obtained when the adhesive is allowed to fully cure. Note that non-flexible paint systems may impair the elasticity of the adhesive and lead to cracking of the paint film.
    - Colour variations may occur due to exposure to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation (especially with the colour shade white). However, a change in colour is purely of aesthetic nature and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
    - Always use Sikaflex®-116 High Grab in conjunction with mechanical fixings for overhead applications or heavy items.
    - For very heavy items provide temporary support until Sikaflex®-116 High Grab has fully cured.
    - Full surface applications / fixings are not recommended since the inner part of the adhesive layer may never cure.
    - Before using on reconstituted, cast or natural stone, contact Sika Technical Services.
    - Do not use on bituminous substrates, natural rubber, EPDM rubber or on any building materials which might leach oils, plasticisers or solvents that could degrade the adhesive.
    - Do not use on polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE / Teflon), and certain plasticised synthetic materials. Preliminary trials are recommended or contact Sika® Technical Services.
    - Do not use for glass bonding if the bond line is exposed to sunlight.
    - Do not use for structural bonding.
    - Do not expose uncured Sikaflex®-116 High Grab to alcohol containing products as this may interfere with the curing reaction.
4.7 Further information.
    - Pre-treatment Chart Sealing and Bonding

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C min. / +40 °C max.
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C min. / +40 °C max. Minimum +3 °C above dew point temperature
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.6):
    - For optimum workability, the recommended adhesive temperature is +20 °C.
    - Application during high temperature changes is not recommended (movement during the curing).
    - Colour variations may occur due to exposure to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation (especially with the colour shade white). However, a change in colour is purely of aesthetic nature and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: ~1.40 kg/l (ISO 1183-1)
    - Shore A hardness: ~45 (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Tensile strength: ~2.2 N/mm² (ISO 37)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~500 % (ISO 37)
    - Tear propagation resistance: ~7.0 N/mm (ISO 34)
    - Sag flow: 0 mm (20 mm profile, 23 °C) (ISO 7390)
    - Curing rate: ~3 mm/24 hours (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.); *Sika Corporate Quality Procedure (CQP* 049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~20 min (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikaflex®-116 High Grab, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/v/sikaflex-116-highgrab.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikaflex 116 High Grab, version 09/04/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/u/MSDS%20Sikaflex-116%20High%20Grab%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikaflex®-116 High Grab, version 09/03/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sds-sikaflex-116highgrab.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
